body:
Jasmine Liu: Hey all — as we ramp regulated POCs from the ABM pilot, we need a consistent CS/SE handoff template so we don’t drop context between discovery → POC → security review → success plan.

Jasmine Liu: Drafting a 1-pager to live in the POC folder + pasted into the HubSpot “Implementation Notes” field. Can folks react/ reply with what *must* be captured for regulated (FinServ/Healthcare) so CS isn’t chasing basics later?

Markus Klein: +1. We keep re-learning the same stuff (VPC connectivity, audit log exports, retention expectations) account to account.

Rachel Kim: Agree. For CS, the big misses have been: clear success criteria (latency/throughput) + who owns what on the customer side (security vs platform) + comms cadence.

Fatima Noor: Adding: exact data classification + boundaries. “No PHI leaves customer VPC” vs “de-identified text only” etc. People are squishy in calls and it bites us.

Simran Kaur: Also need deployment mode explicitly: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem). If Private, what’s the network pattern (peering, PrivateLink, etc) + who manages DNS/TLS certs.

Jasmine Liu: Cool. Here’s my current outline (WIP). What should I add/remove?

Jasmine Liu: 
1) Account + POC basics
- Company / opportunity link
- POC start/end dates
- Deployment mode: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC) / On-prem
- Region/data residency requirement

2) Success criteria (measurable)
- Primary use case(s)
- Latency target (p50/p95)
- Throughput target (req/s or tok/s)
- Cost target (if they gave one)
- “Definition of Done” for POC → next stage

3) Stakeholders (names + roles + decision power)
- Exec sponsor
- Platform/Infra owner
- ML owner
- Security/GRC
- Legal/Procurement

4) Current architecture + constraints
- Inbound/outbound network rules
- Allowed egress domains/IPs
- Auth requirements
- Observability/SIEM integration

5) Risks / open questions
- Risk log + mitigation + owner

6) Comms + cadence
- Weekly status call owner
- Slack/Email channel
- Escalation path

Markus Klein: Looks good. In (4) add: “customer-managed KMS/HSM?” and “key ownership model” (BYOK / CMK) because security will ask, and it changes implementation details.

Olga Petrov: Please capture “evidence requested / provided” at minimum. When we get security questionnaires mid-POC, we need an audit trail of what we shared + under what conditions (NDA in place, etc).

Kevin Osei: +1 to Olga. Also a field for “approved security artifacts shared” so we don’t freestyle language. Eg: SOC2 report under NDA, security FAQ addendum, retention/residency statement.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. Also include “customer control requirements” vs “nice-to-have.” For regulated, the top gating controls are usually:
- Audit logs (what events, export path)
- Retention configuration (prompts/outputs/logs)
- Access controls (SSO/RBAC)
- Encryption + key management
- Data residency
If we note which of these are hard requirements upfront, we can prevent the POC from drifting.

Rachel Kim: Can we add a section for “Customer responsibilities vs Redwood responsibilities” (esp for Private)? Otherwise CS gets asked to own customer-side infra.

Simran Kaur: +100. Maybe a mini RACI table (even just bullets):
- Networking (VPC peering / routes / SGs)
- GPU capacity (Redwood vs customer)
- Logging pipeline (who stands up SIEM sink)
- Key management integrations

Tyler Benson: From ops side: if we’re pasting into HubSpot, can we standardize the headings exactly? Makes it easier to parse/search later. Also we can create a snippet/template in HubSpot.

Jasmine Liu: Good call. I’ll standardize headings + make a HubSpot “snippet” version.

Fatima Noor: Don’t forget “data handling assumptions” as an explicit checkbox line:
- No training on customer data
- Prompts/outputs storage: yes/no + where
- Redaction/de-identification: done by customer vs Redwood
- Any PHI/PCI present

Olga Petrov: Please phrase carefully: “no training” is fine, but storage/retention must match our approved posture (esp for hosted logs). Capture what’s *required*, not what we promise ad hoc.

Jasmine Liu: Yep — I’ll keep it as “Customer requirement / question” + “approved answer link” rather than writing new policy text.

Markus Klein: Another field: “POC traffic shape.” Batch vs streaming, avg prompt length, max context. This impacts sizing + whether continuous batching/caching is required.

Rachel Kim: And “timeline dependencies”: security review date, procurement lead time, any internal change freeze on customer side.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Add “incident response expectations” (who to notify, time window). Some regulated teams want to confirm IR contacts during POC.

Kevin Osei: I can drop in links to the two security FAQ addenda + the retention/residency positioning doc once Jasmine shares the template doc.

Jasmine Liu: Great. Proposed final template sections (v0.2):

A) POC Snapshot
- Opportunity link, POC dates, deployment mode, region/residency

B) Use Case + Success Criteria
- Use case(s)
- Measurable perf/cost targets
- Acceptance test (what dataset/traffic they’ll run)

C) Stakeholder Map
- Names, roles, decision maker, approvals needed (Security/Legal/Proc)

D) Architecture + Integrations
- Network pattern (PrivateLink/peering), DNS/TLS owner
- Auth (SSO, API keys), RBAC needs
- Logging/audit export + SIEM target
- KMS/HSM/BYOK requirement

E) Data Handling + Compliance Requirements (capture as requirements + links)
- Data classification (PHI/PCI/PII)
- Retention requirements (prompts/outputs/logs)
- Audit logging requirements (events + retention + export)
- Evidence requested/provided + NDA status

F) RACI (Customer vs Redwood)
- Networking, infra, keys, logging pipeline

G) Risks / Open Questions
- Risk, impact, owner, mitigation, due date

H) Comms Cadence
- Weekly call, status doc link, escalation contacts

Jasmine Liu: If no objections, I’ll publish a Google Doc + HubSpot snippet by EOD and start using it for the next 2 regulated POCs. :thumbsup:

Rachel Kim: :thumbsup: Works for CS.

Markus Klein: :thumbsup: + I’ll ask SE team to adopt it for POC kickoff notes.

Olga Petrov: :thumbsup: Please include a “Last updated” line + owner, so we know who to ping.

Kevin Osei: :thumbsup: Send me the doc link once it’s live.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: :thumbsup: Happy to review the compliance section for wording / pointers.

Tyler Benson: Once it’s final, I’ll convert to a HubSpot snippet + add a property checklist reminder for the team.
